# schemagx

> Inspect a relational schema for dangling keys, foreign-key cycles and dead tables. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes an annotated storyboard.

schemagx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. Declare tables,
primary keys and foreign keys; `schemagx inspect` checks every reference
resolves, finds foreign-key cycles, and points at dead tables.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/schemagx" schemagx --help
uv tool install ./packages/schemagx      # from a clone
```

Needs Python 3.10+ and Pillow.

## Use

```sh
schemagx inspect schema.py            # report + storyboard, exit 1 on any error
schemagx inspect schema.py --json
schemagx inspect schema.py --no-storyboard
schemagx render  schema.py -o schema.png
```

A schema file defines `schema` (a `Schema`) or module-level `TABLES` /
`PRIMARY_KEYS` / `FOREIGN_KEYS` / `ROOTS`. Foreign keys are `"table.column"`
strings pointing child -> parent.

Or point it at SQL DDL: `schemagx inspect schema.sql` reads `CREATE TABLE`,
`PRIMARY KEY` and `FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES` as the same model. A composite
key, or any statement that is not `CREATE TABLE`, exits 2 with its line rather
than being guessed at. Column types are compared by family, so a `SERIAL` key
with an `INTEGER` reference is not a mismatch.

## Checks

error: `dangling-foreign-key`, `dangling-reference` (a root that names no table).
warn: `fk-type-mismatch`, `fk-to-non-primary-key`, `cyclic-foreign-key`.
info: `missing-primary-key`, `orphan-table`, `no-tables`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
